items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: So he hired John Anderson and me and Red Callender and Oscar Bradley.

ctx.x: Erroll Garner formed a trio later with Harold "Doc" West and Red Callender and him, and I was on some sets with them.

I also played with Art Tatum for the first time during that period. He was working at a place called the St. Francis down on Eighth Street, and he came to town and he wanted some horns to play with him -- because he always did a single or a trio, you know, a duo... So he hired John Anderson and me and Red Callender and Oscar Bradley. And that was quite an experience, you know. As great as he was, when he played with us, he was like a little kid -- he was so enthused, you know. He just worked and worked and played…

items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: Teddy Edwards, Warren Bracken on piano, Bill Douglas I think was on drums in that band

ctx.x: Who else was in that band?

Teddy Edwards, Warren Bracken on piano, Bill Douglas I think was on drums in that band, and I had a trumpet player, Eddie...I can't think of his name at the moment either... Anyhow, I think there was about a six-piece band with two basses, which may have been ridiculous, but I liked it.
I wish I could have heard it.
